Certificates, university entrance qualification, matriculation certificate and other proof

Review of the submitted documents and expert opinions
First selection interview with a Vertrauensdozent:in, producing an expert opinion
Second selection interview with a member of the selection committee
Final decision by the selection committee, which meets eight to ten times a year
Particular consideration of first-generation students, people with a migration background, women, students at universities of applied sciences and STEM subjects

official.application_route: Online application form on fes.de for the Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen, followed by two selection interviews
official.study_mode: Full-time (part-time and extra-occupational study is not funded)
official.citizenship_residency: Open to foreign nationals; applications are formally possible both from Germany and from abroad, while the English summary page states applicants must already be studying in Germany at a German university
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is explicitly for foreign nationals
official.description: The Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung's basic funding programme for international students supports Bachelor's, Master's, Diplom and Staatsexamen degree programmes at German public or state-recognised universities; the published monthly support is 992 Euro, health insurance costs are covered and scholarship holders with children receive an additional 255 Euro per month.

not_confirmed: study_mode as an explicit published rule (only the exclusion of part-time and extra-occupational study is published)
verification.notes: Amount, health-insurance cover and the 255 Euro child supplement confirmed on the FES programme page; the application steps, document list and 3-7 month decision window confirmed on the FES online application page; the English summary page quotes a 276 Euro family allowance for foreign scholarship holders, a figure not repeated on the German programme page.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a monthly living stipend, not a tuition award: budget for the roughly 992 Euro per month to replace income while health insurance is handled for you. The binding constraint for most applicants is German at B2 or better plus documented socio-political engagement, not grades alone. Apply as early as possible in the degree stage window - a Master's applicant starting in the winter semester must be in by 30 November 2026 - because the whole process, from form to committee decision, runs three to seven months.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International students already enrolled at a German university with strong German, above-average grades and a record of voluntary or political engagement.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are inside the degree-stage window: Master's applicants at the very start of the programme, Bachelor's applicants after semester one and no later than three semesters before the standard study period ends
Assemble first graded transcripts before anything else - without them the application cannot be considered
Document engagement concretely (organisation, role, hours, dates), including any volunteering from your home country if you only recently arrived
Line up two university teachers willing to write references, and give them the FES reference guidance early
Write the motivation letter in German and tie it explicitly to social-democratic values
Diarise travel-cost reimbursement forms for the selection interviews and keep all tickets
common_rejection_risks: Applying before first graded performance records exist, which is an automatic formal barrier for Bachelor's applicants
Treating the German requirement as optional because the degree programme is in English - FES states sufficient German must be proven regardless
Leaving socio-political engagement vague or undocumented, which undercuts the ideelle side of the assessment
Submitting part-time, dual, short (under three semester) or second-degree programmes, which FES explicitly does not fund
Lateness in the degree stage: past the window the application is not considered even with strong grades
Letting references arrive late - FES will not chase them and late documents cannot be considered
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Semester contributions and any tuition charged by your university, rent above what the 992 Euro monthly stipend covers, and living costs for family members beyond the 255 Euro child supplement.
document_audit: Transcripts, matriculation certificate and certificates need to be at hand in the second stage only - the online form comes first and a rejection can arrive before you prepare them
References must come from university teachers; for school-leaver programmes from teachers, so check which category your programme falls into
The CV must explicitly cover socio-political engagement, not just academic history
If you are invited to interviews, travel costs are reimbursable only on the official FES form
alerts: The German programme page and the English summary page publish different family-allowance figures (255 vs 276 Euro) - verify with the FES contact staff before budgeting
Master's summer-semester applicants face a 31 May cut-off, much earlier than most students expect
A 403-style rejection at the online-form stage costs you the whole window, because degree-stage timing cannot be repeated
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online form first, then an e-mail request for documents and references, then two interviews, then a committee decision communicated by e-mail.

official.deadline_central_display: 15 January 2027 (applications close on 15 January or 15 July annually)
official.deadline_note: Two application rounds per year: applications are accepted online on campus.kas.de until 15 January or 15 July.
official.application_cycle: Two rounds annually, closing 15 January and 15 July
official.status_note: The programme page invites applications online on campus.kas.de until 15 January or 15 July annually; the next closing date is 15 January 2027.
benefits: Undergraduate and graduate students: financial support (depending on your income or your parents' income) up to 752 Euros per month plus 300 Euro for study-related expenses (books, writing material etc.)
PhD candidates: financial support of 1350 Euros per month plus 100 Euro for research-related expenses, with further allowances possible
Wide range of seminars on salient political, economic, academic and cultural topics
Access to an extended network of fellow scholarship holders and alumni (over 17,000 alumni)
Individual support and consultations for PhD candidates by the staff of the Graduate Student Support Department and special academic advisors at the university
Career counselling and support with the first steps into the labour market
eligibility: You have completed your schooling and studies with above-average grades
You identify with the political stances represented by the Konrad Adenauer Foundation
You are involved in voluntary work in political, social and cultural areas
You are willing to actively participate in the scholarship programme
You are interested in a broad range of topics beyond your research area and appreciate exchange in a multicultural environment

As a refugee in Germany you are entitled under the specific legal requirements to study and to apply for a scholarship: students with a residence permit under §16 or §18 AufenthG can apply for the international programme (Master's and PhD); students with a residence permit under §24 AufenthG or §61 BAföG can apply for Studienförderung (Bachelor's and Master's) as well as Promotionsförderung (PhD)
requirements: Apply online on campus.kas.de until 15 January or 15 July annually
Upload all required application documents as part of the online application
PhD candidates need a German language certificate at least equivalent to Goethe-Zertifikat C1
documents: Written-out and tabular curriculum vitae of up to three pages
Certified copy of the admission letter from your German university
Letter of assessment of your academic skills (e.g. by a professor at your university)
Copy of the transcript of your university grades and courses (or single course certificates)
Matriculation certificate and copies of all academic diploma and training certificates
Proof of German language skills at B2 level (undergraduate and graduate) or at least Goethe-Zertifikat C1 (PhD)
selection_criteria: Open-mindedness, high commitment and a wide range of interests
Above-average learning or academic achievements at school or university
Social engagement and willingness to assume social and political responsibility
Identification with the foundation's values and views
PhD applicants must have a clear objective, know the current state of research, arguments and methodologies, and have a supervisor familiar with and supporting the proposal
coverage: Up to 752 Euros per month for undergraduate and graduate students, depending on your income or your parents' income
300 Euro for study-related expenses such as books and writing material
1350 Euros per month for PhD candidates plus 100 Euro for research-related expenses (further allowances possible)
application_method: Confirm which programme route your residence permit qualifies you for (Studienförderung, Promotionsförderung or the international programme)
Register and apply online on campus.kas.de before 15 January or 15 July
Upload the document set for your degree stage (undergraduate/graduate or PhD) within the online application

PhD candidates additionally upload the application form on professional and personal development and engagement, the long and tabular CVs, and the five-to-ten-page project proposal with literature appendix
official.application_route: Online application on campus.kas.de with all documents uploaded before the 15 January or 15 July closing date
official.citizenship_residency: Refugees in Germany entitled under the specific legal requirements to study and to apply for a scholarship: residence permits under §16 or §18 AufenthG for the international programme (Master's and PhD), and §24 AufenthG or §61 BAföG for Studienförderung (Bachelor's and Master's) and Promotionsförderung (PhD)
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scheme targets refugees in Germany holding the specified residence permits
official.research_requirement: PhD candidates must submit a proposal of the PhD project of five to ten pages (1.5 line spacing, 12 pt, literature appendix) covering topical actuality and social or political relevance, the main problems and solution approaches, research design and methods, and a tentative timeframe
official.description: The Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung supports refugee students in Germany holding a qualifying residence permit: undergraduate and graduate students receive financial support of up to 752 Euros per month depending on income plus 300 Euro for study-related expenses, and PhD candidates 1350 Euros per month plus 100 Euro for research-related expenses, applied for online on campus.kas.de until 15 January or 15 July annually.
official.program_type: Foundation scholarship for refugees (Studienförderung and Promotionsförderung)

verification.notes: Direct requests to kas.de returned HTTP 403 and the site's security layer blocked a scripted download, so the official page text (published bilingually in English and Ukrainian) was retrieved through a text-rendering proxy of the same kas.de URL; the amounts, documents, deadlines and residence-permit routes are the awarding body's own published wording.

applicant_utility.summary: Your residence-permit paragraph decides which route you can even apply for, so check that before anything else: §24 or §61 BAföG opens both the Bachelor/Master and the PhD route, while §16/§18 restrict you to the international Master's and PhD programme. The monthly figure is income-tested, so the headline 752 Euro is a ceiling rather than a promise, and the 300 Euro study-expenses top-up applies on top. There are only two chances a year, 15 January and 15 July, so a missed window costs six months, not a week.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Refugees already studying or doing a doctorate in Germany with above-average results, verifiable voluntary engagement and a residence permit under §16, §18, §24 AufenthG or §61 BAföG.
application_readiness_checklist: Photograph or scan your residence permit and confirm the exact paragraph (§16, §18, §24 AufenthG or §61 BAföG) against the programme routes
Get a certified copy of your university admission letter early - it is a mandatory upload
Secure a letter of assessment from a professor at your German university before the round opens
For the PhD route, obtain the C1 German certificate first: no certificate means no application
Prepare the written-out CV (4,000-6,000 characters including spaces) and the tabular CV as separate documents
Ask your supervisor to confirm in writing that they know and support the proposal
common_rejection_risks: Applying through the wrong programme route for your residence-permit paragraph
Uploading an uncertified or translated admission letter instead of a certified copy
Submitting an assessment letter older than six months (PhD route) or a proposal the supervisor does not visibly support
Missing the strict character limits and formatting rules for the PhD CV and proposal
Weak documentation of voluntary work, which is an explicit expectation rather than a nice-to-have
Arriving at the 15 January or 15 July date with the portal upload incomplete
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any tuition or semester contributions charged by your university, plus whatever share of living costs exceeds the income-tested monthly amount.
document_audit: Certified copies are required for the admission letter and examination certificates - plain scans are not enough
The tabular and written-out CVs are two separate documents, both required for PhD applicants
The PhD proposal needs a literature appendix and explicit formatting (five to ten pages, 1.5 line spacing, 12 pt)
Two assessment letters are required for the PhD route, and you submit them yourself
alerts: The amount depends on your or your parents' income, so the same profile can produce different awards
PhD applicants must hold a C1 certificate at application time; B2 evidence is only accepted for undergraduate and graduate applicants
The page is published in English and Ukrainian only, while the application itself must be completed in German on campus.kas.de
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One online application on campus.kas.de per round with every document attached, then KAS internal review against the published criteria.
